  Findings

  HIGH     F1   sshd is open to any source on 22/tcp                                              -5
                IPv4: accepted by filter/INPUT rule #7.
                filter/INPUT #7:  -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
                fix  If the clients are known, accept only their addresses. If SSH must stay open to
                     any source, limit new connections for each source: the limit counts every
                     source by itself, so one client cannot lock out the others, and it does not
                     touch established sessions.
                     Replace the rule with one for the known clients:
                       iptables -R INPUT 7 -s <trusted-cidr> -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
                     Or drop the connections of a source that opens more than 10 a minute, in front
                     of the rule:
                       iptables -I INPUT 7 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4 -j DROP

  LOW      F2   nginx is open to any source on 80/tcp                                             -1

                filter/INPUT #8:  -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
                fix  If the clients are known, accept only their addresses.
                     Replace the rule with one for the known clients:
